lineage_attempts.finding: The Evolver saw the 50/51 observation but the feedback bundle did not expose the tested parent skill as a readable candidate source.

The parent source was visible, but the feedback round still inherited the first-round COORDINATED_BREADTH decision contract; a terminal decision-schema failure was followed by ambiguous cleaned-lifecycle restart attempts.
Under the LINEAGE_REFINEMENT contract, the Evolver inspected the parent skill, refined only its canonical-label rule, passed admission and skill smoke, and selected the 13F target.

observed_failures: the predicted canonical label was still not uniform for the same CUSIP

selection.reason: The candidate did not beat its current parent and did not fully realize its predicted label-consistency transition.

scale_findings: A feedback bundle must include the exact parent component source that produced the scored Worker observation.
Lineage refinement requires a different decision contract from first-round cross-task breadth discovery.
Short probes measure activation and completion distance, not final score, on long-tail tasks.
Promotion must remain serialized and score-backed; mechanism evidence alone may justify archiving or a bounded confirm, not automatic promotion.
Large JSONL trace lines should be excerpted around matches to control Evolver context cost.
claim_boundary: This validates one complete refine, target, and rollback path plus several observed setup repairs. It does not show an improved promoted parent, repeat stability, protection transfer, or sealed main-experiment gain.
